name: Making graph models work in real conditions
gist: Papers addressing practical challenges like handling missing data, domain shift, adversarial robustness, and personalizing models for different scenarios in graph learning.
explain: Academic papers test models on clean graphs, but the real world is messy. In production, you face missing data (sensors fail, records are incomplete), distribution shift (the network changes over time or between domains), adversarial attacks (someone deliberately adds edges to fool the model), and the need to personalize (different users need different recommendations). A model trained on one social network may not work on another. A graph model trained on historical data may fail when the network structure changes.

These problems are hard because graph models are sensitive to structure. Remove one node or edge and the entire message-passing process changes. If the model learned to rely on certain neighbor types that disappear in a new domain, it fails. An adversary can deliberately add connections to make normal-looking fraudulent nodes. And personalization means you can't just train one model for everyone—you need to adapt to local structure around each user or entity.

Papers develop techniques for model reliability: training models that still work if data is missing, using data augmentation (carefully adding or removing edges to make the model less brittle), certifying that models resist adversarial attacks. They tackle domain adaptation: training on one graph and transferring to another despite structural differences, sometimes using contrastive learning or unsupervised methods that work without labels in the new domain. They study heterophily (when similar nodes are NOT connected, which breaks standard message-passing), federated learning (training on multiple graphs without centralizing data), and personalization (learning per-user or per-entity models that adapt to local structure).

papers.title: EvA: Evolutionary Attacks on Graphs
papers.contribution: EvA achieves approximately 11% additional accuracy drop on average compared to best previous attacks, can reduce effectiveness of robustness certificates and break conformal sets, scaling to larger graphs with reduced memory.

papers.title: GP2F: Cross-Domain Graph Prompting with Adaptive Fusion of Pre-trained Graph Neural Networks
papers.contribution: GP2F outperforms existing GPL methods on cross-domain few-shot node and graph classification through adaptive fusion under topology constraints.

papers.title: Robustness in Text-Attributed Graph Learning: Insights, Trade-offs, and New Defenses
papers.contribution: Analysis reveals inherent robustness trade-offs between text and structure, performance dependence on text encoders and attack types, and introduces SFT-auto for superior balanced robustness.

papers.title: Temporal Graph Thumbnail: Robust Representation Learning with Global Evolutionary Skeleton
papers.contribution: TGT achieves superior capability and robustness compared to baselines, particularly in rapidly evolving and noisy environments.

papers.title: BOCLOAK: Optimal Transport-Guided Adversarial Attacks on Graph Neural Network-Based Bot Detection
papers.contribution: Achieves up to 80.13% higher attack success rates while using 99.80% less GPU memory under real-world constraints.

papers.title: Homophily-Heterogeneity Gradient Surgery for Federated Graph Learning
papers.contribution: FedGCM achieves superior performance on both homophilous and heterophilous graphs without augmenting client-side burden and includes formal convergence analysis.

papers.title: Learning Adaptive Distribution Alignment with Neural Characteristic Function for Graph Domain Adaptation
papers.contribution: On 10 datasets and 16 transfer tasks, ADAlign outperforms baselines by flexibly capturing multi-order feature-structure dependencies without manual specification.

papers.title: Oversmoothing, "Oversquashing'', Heterophily, Long-Range, and more: Demystifying Common Beliefs in Graph Machine Learning
papers.contribution: Work promotes critical thinking and clarifies distinctions between different graph learning issues, helping researchers address more clearly defined and targeted problems.

papers.title: Progressive Graph Structure Adjustment for Homophily Shift Adaptation
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines with particularly large gains under severe homophily mismatch, highlighting importance of explicit homophily alignment.

papers.title: SAGA: Structural Aggregation Guided Alignment with Dynamic View and Neighborhood Order Selection for Multiview Graph Domain Adaptation
papers.contribution: Effectively characterizes and mitigates both view-level and hop-level structural discrepancies through dynamic alignment.
